meta.title: About Us | MyJudicial
meta.description: Learn about MyJudicial, Rwanda's premier platform connecting clients with verified legal experts.

hero.title: Democratizing Access to Justice Across Rwanda
hero.subtitle: We bridge the gap between citizens, businesses, and certified legal advocates—combining Bar accreditation, upfront pricing, and modern technology.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.text: To democratize access to justice in Rwanda by providing a transparent, efficient, and secure platform that connects individuals and businesses with verified legal professionals.
mission.visionText: To become the leading digital legal infrastructure in Africa, where finding a lawyer is as easy as booking a flight, and legal processes are streamlined for maximum efficiency.

story.title: Our Story
story.subtitle: Bridging Rwanda's legal gap with trust, technology, and transparency.
story.text1: MyJudicial was born out of a simple observation: finding the right lawyer in Rwanda was often complicated, opaque, and intimidating for the average person or small business.
story.text2: We realized that by leveraging technology, we could bridge the gap between talented legal professionals and those who need their services. Today, MyJudicial is a comprehensive ecosystem that not only helps clients find lawyers but also provides lawyers with the tools they need to manage and grow their practice.

access.title: Access
access.text: We believe everyone deserves access to quality legal representation, regardless of their background or connections.

transparency.title: Transparency
transparency.text: Clear, upfront pricing with no hidden fees. You always know what you're paying for before you commit.

trust.title: Trust
trust.text: Every lawyer on our platform is strictly vetted and verified. Your payments and data are always secure.

compliance.title: Privacy & Legal Privilege
compliance.text: Operating in strict compliance with Law No. 058/2021 on Personal Data Protection, with encrypted consultations preserving client privilege.

ecosystem.title: Built with Rwanda's Legal & Financial Institutions
ecosystem.subtitle: MyJudicial collaborates with accredited institutions across Rwanda to ensure professional standards and seamless escrow execution.

disclaimer.title: Regulatory Notice
disclaimer.text: MyJudicial is an independent technology platform connecting clients with accredited Rwanda Bar Association advocates. MyJudicial is not a law firm and does not provide legal representation directly.

verification.title: The 4-Stage Advocate Verification Protocol
verification.subtitle: Every advocate on MyJudicial passes a documented, audited review before their profile goes live.
verification.stage1Desc: A government-issued ID and an active Rwanda Bar Association (RBA) licence are collected and checked by our review team before any profile is drafted.
verification.stage2Desc: Registration details are cross-referenced against the official RBA Roll of Advocates to confirm the advocate is in good standing.
verification.stage3Desc: Advocates agree to published fixed fees, escrow terms, and the platform code of conduct before offering consultations.
verification.stage4Desc: A final human review approves the published profile. Every step of the process is written to an audit log.

milestones.title: Our Journey
milestones.subtitle: From a simple matching idea to a governed marketplace, built in public.
milestones.item1Desc: MyJudicial starts with a simple observation: finding a lawyer in Rwanda should not be opaque, slow, or intimidating.
milestones.item2Desc: The advocate verification protocol and fee escrow are built, so credentials and payments are protected by default.
milestones.item3Desc: A trilingual public platform ships with secure video consultations and AI-assisted case triage for clients across Rwanda.

governance.title: Institutional Governance & Ethics
governance.subtitle: Clear rules that keep the marketplace fair for clients and advocates alike.
governance.rule1Desc: A paid consultation fee is held in escrow and released to the advocate only after the consultation is completed, or refunded on cancellation.
governance.rule2Desc: Published fees are fixed and tied to a single consultation. There are no hidden charges, and disputes follow a documented process.
governance.rule3Desc: Consultations are private, limited to the booked participants, and never recorded. Data is handled under Rwanda Law No. 058/2021.

item1.q: How do I choose and book a verified advocate on MyJudicial?
item1.a: Browse our directory by practice area, language, or location, or describe your situation to our AI Legal Assistant for instant triage. Select an advocate, pick an available calendar slot, and confirm your booking with escrow protection.

item2.q: What languages do advocates on MyJudicial consult in?
item2.a: All advocates are fluent in at least two of Rwanda's official legal languages. You can filter and consult in Kinyarwanda, English, or French to ensure complete clarity and comfort.

item3.q: I live in the Rwandan diaspora. Can I consult an advocate about land, succession, or business?
item3.a: Yes. You can pay with international credit or debit cards, schedule consultations across international time zones, and meet via our encrypted in-browser video room to review land certificates (UPI), business contracts, or succession files.

item4.q: Do I need to download Zoom, Teams, or an app to join the video consultation?
item4.a: No. Our consultation room runs 100% inside your web browser using LiveKit WebRTC. You do not need to download or install any external software on your computer or phone.

item5.q: Can the advocate represent me in court after our online consultation?
item5.a: Yes. Online consultations serve as an initial diagnostic session. If your case requires litigation, your advocate can issue an official retainer agreement (convention d'honoraires) and power of attorney (procuration) to represent you before Rwandan courts via the IECMS.

item6.q: How and when do advocates receive consultation payouts?
item6.a: Payouts are automated and guaranteed. Once you conclude the consultation and submit the session brief, the escrow balance is released immediately to your registered MTN Mobile Money, Airtel Money, or Rwandan commercial bank account.

item7.q: Do advocates retain full autonomy over their consultation rates and schedule?
item7.a: Yes. In accordance with Rwanda Bar Association standards, advocates independently set their consultation fees and configure their available hours. MyJudicial does not fix prices or impose mandatory tariffs.

item8.q: How is my Rwanda Bar Association (RBA) accreditation vetted?
item8.a: Every advocate is verified against the official Rwanda Bar Association Roll, practicing certificate, and National ID before their profile is published. Only advocates in active good standing are admitted.

item9.q: What happens if a client fails to attend the scheduled consultation?
item9.a: Your professional time is protected. If a client fails to attend without cancelling at least 24 hours in advance, the consultation fee held in escrow is disbursed to the advocate in accordance with platform cancellation policy.

item10.q: How does the regulated escrow system protect my money?
item10.a: When you book a consultation, your payment is held safely in a regulated escrow custody account. The advocate is only paid after the consultation has concluded satisfactorily. If a session is cancelled or the advocate does not attend, your funds are refunded.

item11.q: Which payment methods are accepted on MyJudicial?
item11.a: We accept MTN Mobile Money and Airtel Money for local payments, as well as Visa and Mastercard debit and credit cards for domestic and international clients.

item12.q: Are there any hidden fees, platform surcharges, or extra invoices?
item12.a: No. The consultation fee displayed on the advocate's profile is the total, final amount. There are no hidden booking fees, subscription traps, or unexpected charges.

item13.q: What is the refund and cancellation policy?
item13.a: Clients can reschedule or cancel a consultation for a full refund up to 24 hours before the scheduled time. If an advocate fails to join a session, the client receives a 100% immediate escrow refund.

item14.q: Are all lawyers on MyJudicial accredited by the Rwanda Bar Association?
item14.a: Yes. Every single legal expert on MyJudicial is an accredited advocate cross-checked against the official Rwanda Bar Association Roll. We do not allow unverified third parties to offer legal counsel.

item15.q: Is my consultation recorded by the platform?
item15.a: No. We never record video or audio consultations. All sessions use peer-to-peer encrypted WebRTC to preserve strict legal professional secrecy and attorney-client privilege.

item16.q: How does MyJudicial comply with Rwandan Data Protection Law No. 058/2021?

faqs.clientQ1: I am in the Rwandan diaspora (USA, Europe, EAC). Can I consult an advocate about land or business in Rwanda?
faqs.clientA1: Yes. A substantial portion of our clients reside abroad in the diaspora. You can pay with international credit or debit cards, schedule consultations across international time zones, and meet your advocate via our encrypted in-browser video room to review land titles (UPI), commercial contracts, or succession documents.
faqs.clientQ2: What languages do advocates on MyJudicial speak?
faqs.clientA2: All advocates on MyJudicial are fluent in at least two of Rwanda's official legal languages. You can filter and consult in Kinyarwanda, English, or French, ensuring you can explain your situation in the language you feel most comfortable with.
faqs.clientQ3: Do I need to download Zoom, Teams, or an app to join the consultation?
faqs.clientA3: No. Our consultation room runs 100% inside your web browser (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge) using LiveKit WebRTC. You do not need to install software, sign up for third-party accounts, or download any plugins on your computer or mobile phone.
faqs.clientQ4: How does the direct telephone consultation work if my internet is weak?
faqs.clientA4: If you choose the Phone Consultation modality, you do not need an internet connection. At the scheduled consultation time, the advocate will place a direct carrier telephone call to the verified MTN or Airtel mobile number you provided during booking.
faqs.clientQ5: Can I upload land title documents (UPI), contracts, or court summons before the call?
faqs.clientA5: Yes. During the intake process, you can securely upload PDF documents, scanned deeds, or photo evidence. Your advocate has confidential access to these files prior to the session, ensuring they arrive fully prepared rather than spending billable consultation minutes reading documents.
faqs.clientQ6: Can the advocate represent me in court after our online consultation?
faqs.clientA6: Yes. Online consultations frequently lead to full legal representation. If your matter requires courtroom litigation, contract drafting, or negotiation, the advocate will provide an official engagement agreement (convention d'honoraires) and power of attorney (procuration) to represent you before Rwandan courts via the Integrated Electronic Case Management System (IECMS).
faqs.advocateQ1: How and when do advocates receive consultation payouts?
faqs.advocateA1: Payouts are automated and guaranteed. Once you conclude the consultation and submit the session brief, the escrow balance is released immediately to your registered MTN Mobile Money, Airtel Money, or Rwandan commercial bank account—eliminating billing friction and unpaid invoices.
faqs.advocateQ2: Do I retain full autonomy over my consultation rates and schedule?
faqs.advocateA2: Yes. In accordance with Rwanda Bar Association standards, advocates independently set their consultation fees and configure their available hours. MyJudicial does not fix prices or impose mandatory tariffs.
faqs.advocateQ3: How is my Rwanda Bar Association (RBA) accreditation vetted?
faqs.advocateA3: Every advocate is verified against the official Rwanda Bar Association Roll, practicing certificate, and National ID before their profile is published. Only advocates in active good standing are admitted to the marketplace.
faqs.advocateQ4: Can I convert an online consultation into a formal litigation or retainer mandate?
faqs.advocateA4: Yes. Online consultations serve as an initial discovery session. When a case requires litigation, contract drafting, or administrative proceedings, you can issue an official engagement agreement (convention d'honoraires) and power of attorney (procuration) to represent the client before Rwandan courts via the IECMS.
faqs.advocateQ5: What happens if a client fails to attend the scheduled consultation?
faqs.advocateA5: Your professional time is protected. If a client fails to attend without cancelling at least 24 hours in advance, the consultation fee held in escrow is disbursed to the advocate in accordance with platform cancellation policy.
faqs.advocateQ6: How does MyJudicial maintain legal professional privilege and confidentiality?
faqs.advocateA6: All video and audio communications use peer-to-peer 256-bit encrypted WebRTC without platform eavesdropping or automated recording. Client data and uploaded evidence comply strictly with Law No. 058/2021 relating to the protection of personal data and Rwanda Bar confidentiality ethics.

3. Information We Collect
sections.text:
We collect only personal data necessary to provide our digital legal marketplace services. We categorize collected information into the following categories:

• Account & Authentication Data: Full legal name, email address, telephone number, one-way hashed passwords (Argon2/bcrypt), federated OAuth account IDs (Google, LinkedIn), preferred language, and account role (Citizen, Expert, Admin).
• Advocate & Legal Expert Professional Data: Display name, professional biography, law firm affiliation, physical office address, Rwanda Bar Association (RBA) roll number, active practicing certificate, national ID/passport copy, academic diplomas, verified legal specialties, consultation fee rates, and Mobile Money payout phone numbers.
• Consultation & Booking Records: Selected legal service category, consultation delivery mode (video, phone, in-person), appointment date and duration, client intake summary notes, meeting room identifiers, and reschedule/cancellation history.
• In-Platform Communications: Direct messages exchanged between clients and legal advocates, file attachments (PDFs, court notices, contracts), and message delivery timestamps.
• Legal Vault Documents: Confidential case files, contracts, pleadings, deeds, and identification documents uploaded to the user vault. Files are encrypted client-side using AES-256-GCM before storage in OCI Object Storage.
• Financial & Escrow Records: Mobile Money transaction references (MTN Mobile Money, Airtel Money), AzamPay gateway transaction identifiers, platform commission calculations, escrow deposit and payout ledger records. MyJudicial does NOT store debit/credit card numbers or Mobile Money PINs.
• AI Triage Inquiries: Case descriptions submitted in text or voice audio, in-memory transcriptions, detected legal specialties, urgency assessments, and estimated budget parameters.
• Location Data: Geolocation coordinates provided on-demand for map discovery (defaults to Kigali Central Business District: -1.9441, 30.0619); advocate office coordinates.
• Technical & Audit Logs: IP addresses, browser user agent strings, login records, and immutable audit logs (AuditLog) tracking sensitive platform events.

sections.title: 4. How We Collect Your Information
sections.text:
We collect personal data through transparent, direct, and automated mechanisms:

• Directly Provided by You: When creating an account, filling out profile fields, submitting intake forms, uploading documents to the vault, exchanging messages, or paying consultation fees.
• Automated Interactions: During your navigation of the platform, essential cookies, device attributes, IP addresses, and diagnostic error telemetry are automatically recorded to ensure system integrity and security.
• Legal Expert Submissions: When advocates apply to join MyJudicial, submitting professional credentials, Bar certificates, identification, and schedule rules.
• Official Verification Cross-Checks: To ensure trust and consumer protection, our compliance team cross-checks submitted credentials directly against the public Roll of Advocates maintained by the Rwanda Bar Association.

sections.title: 5. Purposes & How We Use Your Data
sections.text:
MyJudicial processes personal data exclusively for the following specified, legitimate purposes:

• Marketplace Operation & Account Management: Administering user registrations, authentication, role authorization, and user profile management.
• Advocate Verification & Fraud Prevention: Verifying advocate Bar standing, preventing unauthorized representation, and safeguarding consumer trust.
• Booking & Virtual Consultations: Facilitating appointment scheduling, calendar synchronization, and establishing secure WebRTC video rooms via LiveKit.
• Escrow & Financial Settlement: Holding consultation fee deposits in escrow custody and executing disbursements to legal experts upon verified consultation delivery.
• Encrypted Document Vault Services: Providing high-security, client-side encrypted cloud storage for legal documentation and case evidence.
• AI-Assisted Intake Triage & Case Classification: Providing automated legal subject-matter classification, urgency assessment, and lawyer matchmaking based on public practice areas.
• Operational Notifications & Service Messaging: Dispatching appointment reminders, authentication OTPs, payment confirmations, and system notifications via Brevo (SMS and email).
• Platform Security, Auditing & Legal Compliance: Detecting cyber threats, investigating disputes, maintaining immutable audit trails, and satisfying statutory tax and regulatory reporting obligations under Rwandan law.

sections.title: 6. Legal Basis for Processing (Law No. 058/2021)
sections.text:
Pursuant to Article 46 of Rwanda Law No. 058/2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy, MyJudicial processes your personal data under the following lawful bases:

• Performance of a Contract (Article 46(1)(b)): Processing is necessary for the conclusion and performance of the contract between you and MyJudicial (terms of service, booking management, escrow fee custody, document storage, and account access).
• Compliance with a Legal Obligation (Article 46(1)(c)): Processing is necessary to satisfy statutory obligations under Rwandan commercial law, financial record-keeping, anti-money laundering regulations, tax filings with the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA), and lawful judicial summonses.
• Legitimate Interests (Article 46(1)(f)): Processing is necessary for the legitimate business interests of MyJudicial and its users—specifically verifying advocate credentials on the Bar Roll, preventing fraud and unauthorized practice of law, protecting infrastructure security, and maintaining immutable audit trails—provided these interests do not override your fundamental rights.
• Explicit Consent (Article 46(1)(a)): Where applicable, we rely on your specific, informed consent for optional features, including granting device geolocation for interactive map search and uploading voice audio recordings for AI transcription. Consent may be revoked at any time.

sections.title: 7. How We Share Information & Recipients
sections.text:
We do not sell, rent, or monetize your personal data. We disclose personal information solely to the following defined categories of recipients:

• Designated Legal Experts: When you initiate an intake inquiry or confirm a consultation booking, your contact information, issue description, and shared documents are provided directly to that advocate.
• Core Cloud & Hosting Providers:
  - Database & Identity Hosting: Supabase / Amazon Web Services (AWS) data centers.
  - Encrypted Document Vault: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Object Storage with Key Management Service (KMS) envelope encryption.
  - Real-Time Virtual Consultations: LiveKit Cloud infrastructure for encrypted WebRTC video rooms.
  - Transactional Communications: Brevo (formerly Sendinblue) for transactional email, booking alerts, and SMS dispatch.
  - In-Memory Caching & Session Rate-Limiting: Upstash Redis.
  - Payment Gateway & Escrow Aggregation: AzamPay for Mobile Money checkout and automated advocate disbursements.
• Rwanda Bar Association & Regulatory Bodies: In instances of professional misconduct inquiries or credential cross-referencing.
• Judicial Authorities & Law Enforcement: Where strictly mandated under a legally binding court order, subpoena, or statutory warrant issued by a competent Rwandan judicial authority.

sections.title: 8. Client-Lawyer Confidentiality & Legal Privilege
sections.text:
Legal Professional Privilege: Under Rwandan law and the statutory regulations of the Rwanda Bar Association, legal counsel consultations and case materials enjoy statutory professional secrecy (secret professionnel). The advocate you consult is legally bound to preserve the confidentiality of all information disclosed in contemplation of legal representation.

Technical Platform Safeguards: MyJudicial is engineered to uphold this sacred duty. Documents uploaded to the legal vault are encrypted client-side using AES-256-GCM. MyJudicial personnel, support teams, and third-party vendors do not possess access to decrypt or review confidential client-advocate communications or case evidence, except where strictly required for authorized administrative maintenance under audited conditions or when compelled by a valid Rwandan court order.

sections.title: 9. AI-Assisted Features & Machine Learning Transparency
sections.text:
MyJudicial incorporates modern artificial intelligence features through our microservice (myjudicial-ai-service) to streamline case triage and intake:

• Voice Transcription (Whisper): When you record an audio intake note, our local Whisper speech recognition model transcribes the speech to text in-memory. Audio streams are not retained after transcription completes.
• Case Subject-Matter Classification: Our language model (self-hosted Ollama with Qwen2.5 or dedicated enterprise cloud inference) analyzes the factual description of your inquiry to identify primary legal areas (such as Land Law, Family Law, or Commercial Law) and evaluate urgency indicators.
• Semantic Vector Search: The inquiry text is converted into mathematical vector embeddings (using sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2) to match matters against published advocate experience.
• ABSOLUTELY NO MODEL TRAINING: Personal case descriptions, uploaded documents, voice recordings, and consultation data are NEVER used to train, retrain, or improve public or proprietary foundation models.
• Informational Nature: AI triage suggestions are strictly informational tools designed to assist you in navigating the legal marketplace. The AI does NOT provide legal advice, does not draft binding pleadings without advocate review, and never substitutes for a licensed human lawyer.

11. Location Data & Geospatial Search
sections.text:
On-Demand Geolocation: To assist citizens in discovering legal advocates with physical chambers in their vicinity or jurisdiction, MyJudicial offers an interactive map feature. Your browser requests location permission strictly when you click to discover nearby advocates.

Default & Fallback Coordinates: If you decline permission or if your device does not support geolocation, the platform defaults to the central business coordinates of Kigali (Nyarugenge District: -1.9441, 30.0619).

No Background Tracking: Client geographic coordinates are transmitted temporarily to execute a radius distance query against advocate office coordinates (using PostGIS ST_DWithin geospatial functions). Client coordinates are never tracked in the background and are never stored in user account records or profile tables.

sections.title: 12. Cookies & Similar Technologies
sections.text:
Session & Functional Cookies: We utilize strictly necessary cookies to maintain secure authentication sessions (NextAuth session tokens, CSRF tokens, and Supabase auth keys) and remember interface preferences (such as your chosen language: English, French, Kinyarwanda; and theme: light or dark mode).

No Third-Party Ad Trackers: We do not deploy third-party advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.

Dedicated Cookie Policy: For a complete inventory of cookie names, storage lifespans, purposes, and browser control settings, please review our standalone Cookie Policy at /cookies.

sections.title: 13. Data Retention & Archival Governance
sections.text:
Transparent Data Lifecycle: We retain your personal data strictly for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes for which it was collected and to satisfy statutory requirements under Rwandan law:

• Active User Accounts: Identity and account credentials remain active until you delete your account or request account closure.
• Statutory Accounting & Financial Ledgers: Consultation fee transactions, escrow settlement logs, and billing invoices are retained for ten (10) years in compliance with Rwandan tax laws, commercial code regulations, and anti-money laundering requirements.
• Legal Vault Documents: Uploaded case documents remain stored in your private vault until you delete them or close your account.
• Security & System Audit Logs: Audit trails (AuditLog) are maintained for security analysis, forensic investigation, and fraud prevention.
• Data Governance Roadmap: In accordance with supervisory guidance from the Data Protection Office (DPO Rwanda), MyJudicial is actively codifying automated data lifecycle purging jobs to systematically delete staging records upon statutory expiry.

sections.title: 14. Technical & Organizational Security Controls
sections.text:
We implement defense-in-depth security measures to protect your personal data against accidental loss, unauthorized access, alteration, or disclosure:

• Encryption in Transit: All communications between your device and our servers are encrypted using Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.3 / HTTPS).
• Encryption at Rest & Vault Security: Sensitive documents stored in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Object Storage are protected by client-side AES-256-GCM encryption with envelope keys managed via OCI Key Management Service (KMS).
• Password Hashing: User passwords are protected using salted, cryptographic one-way hashes (Argon2/bcrypt); plaintext passwords are never recorded.
• Role-Based Access Controls (RBAC): Strict permission boundaries separate Citizen, Expert, and Administrator capabilities, ensuring platform personnel cannot access confidential user data without specific operational justification.
• Immutable Audit Logging: Security-critical actions (authentication, credential verification, file access, escrow releases) are permanently logged to dedicated audit tables with IP addresses and timestamps.

sections.title: 15. International Data Transfers (Articles 40-42)
16. Your Privacy Rights Under Rwanda Law No. 058/2021
sections.text:
As a data subject under Law No. 058/2021, you are entitled to the following statutory rights regarding your personal information:

• Right to be Informed (Articles 15 & 16): Right to receive clear, concise, and transparent information regarding how your data is processed.
• Right of Access (Article 16): Right to obtain confirmation of whether we hold personal data concerning you and to receive a structured copy of that data.
• Right to Rectification (Article 18): Right to request the immediate correction of inaccurate or incomplete personal data. You may also update your account details directly in Profile Settings.
• Right to Erasure / Deletion (Article 19): Right to request the permanent erasure of your personal data where it is no longer required for the purposes collected or where you withdraw consent, subject to statutory retention obligations under Rwandan tax and commercial laws.
• Right to Restriction of Processing (Article 20): Right to obtain restriction of processing during verification of data accuracy or lawful processing disputes.
• Right to Data Portability (Article 21): Right to receive your personal data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format.
• Right to Object (Article 22): Right to object to processing founded on legitimate interests or direct informational communications.
• Right to Withdraw Consent (Article 46): Where processing is based on consent, you may withdraw consent at any time without retroactive impact.

How to Exercise Your Rights: Submit your request in writing to our Data Protection Officer at {{dpoEmail}}. To safeguard your identity, we may require identity verification prior to acting on your request. We will acknowledge receipt promptly and provide a substantive response within the statutory thirty (30) day timeframe prescribed by Law No. 058/2021.

sections.title: 17. Children's Privacy (Under 18)
sections.text:
Eighteen (18) Age Requirement: The MyJudicial marketplace is strictly intended for individuals who are at least eighteen (18) years of age and possess full legal capacity to enter into binding legal agreements under the laws of Rwanda.

Minors Requiring Legal Services: Pursuant to Article 9 of Law No. 058/2021, personal data of a child can only be processed with the verified consent of a parent or legal guardian. If legal counsel is sought on behalf of a child or minor (e.g. in family matters, inheritance, or protection cases), the consultation must be initiated, authorized, and managed by their lawful parent or legal guardian. If we discover an unsupervised account registered by a child under 18, we will immediately terminate the account and purge the corresponding data.

sections.title: 18. Service Communications & Marketing Preferences
sections.text:
Transactional Messages: We transmit essential operational communications by SMS and email, including appointment reminders, security OTP verification codes, booking confirmations, escrow release notifications, and critical platform security notices. These communications are integral to service fulfillment and account security, and users cannot opt out of transactional notices while their account remains active.

Marketing & Educational Communications: If MyJudicial provides optional informational legal guides, quarterly legal insights, or platform feature announcements, you will be given a clear choice to opt in. Every marketing message contains an immediate unsubscribe link allowing you to opt out at any time without affecting your operational platform access.

sections.title: 19. Third-Party Websites & Integrations
sections.text:
External Platform Boundaries: The MyJudicial website may feature links to external third-party platforms, such as the Rwanda Bar Association (rwanda-bar.org), government portals, judicial dockets, or payment provider authentication gateways.

Independent Privacy Policies: MyJudicial does not exercise control over the information practices or policies of external websites. Following links to third-party domains is conducted at your own discretion, and we strongly encourage you to review the privacy notices of any external site you visit.

sections.title: 20. Data Breach Response & Statutory Notification
sections.text:
Incident Management Protocol: MyJudicial maintains a documented incident response procedure to swiftly detect, isolate, and remediate suspected personal data breaches or unauthorized access events.

48-Hour Supervisory Notification: In compliance with Article 43 of Rwanda Law No. 058/2021, where an incident constitutes a personal data breach, MyJudicial will notify the National Cyber Security Authority / Data Protection Office (NCSA DPO) within forty-eight (48) hours of becoming aware of the breach.

Data Subject Notification: In accordance with Article 44 of Law No. 058/2021, if the breach is likely to result in a high risk to your rights, freedoms, or financial security, we will notify you without undue delay, detailing the nature of the breach, the potential consequences, and the remedial actions taken to safeguard your data.

sections.title: 21. Supervisory Authority Complaints (NCSA / DPO Rwanda)
sections.text:
Internal Escalation: If you have questions or concerns regarding our privacy practices, we invite you to contact our Data Protection Officer first at {{dpoEmail}}.

Statutory Right to Complain: You have the statutory right under Law No. 058/2021 to lodge a formal complaint with Rwanda's designated supervisory authority for data protection:

National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA)
Data Protection Office (DPO)
Official Web Portal: https://dpo.gov.rw

Periodic Revision: We may update this Privacy Policy periodically to reflect technological enhancements, operational changes, or revised supervisory guidance from the Data Protection Office.

Effective Date & Last Updated: The effective date at the top of this document indicates when the current version was promulgated.

sections.title: 1. Introduction & Statutory Scope
sections.text:
MyJudicial Ltd ("MyJudicial", "we", "our", or "us") operates Rwanda's premier digital legal-services marketplace, connecting citizens, entrepreneurs, and institutions with certified, verified legal advocates.

This Cookie Policy explains how and why we utilize HTTP cookies, browser local storage (localStorage), session storage (sessionStorage), and similar web technologies when you visit our website (myjudicial.com) or access our platform services. This policy is established in full compliance with Law No. 058/2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy.

Scope Boundary: This document specifically addresses browser storage and client-side device identifiers. For comprehensive details regarding how we collect, process, safeguard, and retain personal information across our broader legal infrastructure, please refer to our full Privacy Policy.

sections.title: 2. What Are Cookies & Browser Storage Technologies?
sections.text:
Web applications use several standardized browser storage mechanisms to operate securely and reliably:

• HTTP Cookies: Small alphanumeric text files saved on your computer, tablet, or smartphone by a web server. When you navigate between pages or return on a subsequent visit, your browser transmits these cookies back to our domain so that our system can authenticate your identity and maintain security.
• HTML5 Local Storage (localStorage): A client-side key-value storage mechanism embedded in modern browsers. LocalStorage retains specific user preferences—such as your chosen visual theme or language—locally on your device without transmitting data in HTTP request headers.
• HTML5 Session Storage (sessionStorage): A transient storage repository restricted strictly to the lifespan of an active browser tab. All sessionStorage items are instantly wiped when you close the tab or browser window.

sections.title: 3. Our Core Privacy Commitment: Zero Third-Party Tracking
sections.text:
Unlike conventional consumer platforms, MyJudicial is designed from the ground up for strict confidentiality and legal professional integrity:

• NO Third-Party Behavioral Tracking: We do not deploy Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, tracking beacons, or cross-site tracking scripts. Your browsing and inquiry history is never monitored across the web.
• NO Advertising or Marketing Cookies: We do not permit ad networks, data brokers, or commercial marketing partners to place cookies on your device. We do not sell or monetize user data.
• Privacy by Design: We intentionally engineer all marketplace features—including interactive map discovery and virtual video consultations—using open-source and privacy-preserving infrastructure that requires no third-party profiling.

sections.title: 4. Categories of Technologies We Use
sections.text:
MyJudicial relies exclusively on three transparent, necessary categories of web technologies:

• Strictly Necessary Technologies: Essential for the core operation, identity authentication, and cybersecurity of the platform. Without these technologies, user login, encrypted account sessions, and secure consultation bookings cannot function.
• Preference & Localization Technologies: Enable the platform to remember your deliberate user choices—such as your preferred language (English, French, or Kinyarwanda), color theme mode (Light, Dark, or System), and appointment scheduling timezone.
• Functional & Session State Technologies: Temporarily safeguard your navigation state—such as whether the dashboard sidebar is open or auto-saving multi-step onboarding wizard entries to prevent accidental data loss.

sections.title: 7. Third-Party Technical Services & Zero-Cookie Architecture
sections.text:
We audit all external technical dependencies to guarantee they do not place tracking cookies on your device:

• MapLibre GL Vector Maps: Interactive chamber location maps use open-source MapLibre GL with self-hosted vector tiles. No Google Maps cookies or Mapbox tracking identifiers are placed on your browser.
• LiveKit WebRTC Virtual Consultations: Video consultations are powered by LiveKit Cloud using end-to-end encrypted WebSockets and WebRTC peer channels. LiveKit operates without placing persistent tracking cookies.
• Artificial Intelligence Triage: Case triage inquiries are processed in-memory through our secure backend microservice. AI interactions set no client-side cookies or advertising trackers.
• Supabase Realtime: WebSockets are utilized exclusively for real-time messaging and notification dispatch without setting persistent third-party cookies.

sections.title: 8. Legal Basis & Consent Under Law No. 058/2021
sections.text:
Statutory Lawful Basis: Under Article 46 of Law No. 058/2021, the processing of data via strictly necessary cookies is justified by Contractual Performance (Article 46(1)(b)) and Legitimate Interests (Article 46(1)(f)) to secure platform infrastructure, authenticate accounts, and prevent fraud.

User-Requested Preferences: Preference cookies (such as language selection and theme mode) are stored strictly pursuant to your deliberate user requests to tailor the interface.

Why No Consent Banner Is Displayed: Because MyJudicial deploys ZERO non-essential advertising, targeting, or third-party profiling cookies, Rwandan and international data protection laws do not mandate an obstructive cookie banner. Should we ever introduce optional analytical or marketing tools in the future, we will deploy an explicit, prior-consent preference center before any such cookies are loaded.

sections.title: 9. How to Control, Inspect & Disable Cookies in Your Browser
sections.text:
You have full technical control over cookies stored on your device. Every modern web browser provides settings allowing you to view, manage, block, or delete cookies:

• Google Chrome: Settings → Privacy and security → Third-party cookies → See all site data and permissions.
• Mozilla Firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → Cookies and Site Data → Manage Data.
• Apple Safari: Settings → Safari → Advanced → Privacy → Block all cookies.
• Microsoft Edge: Settings → Cookies and site permissions → Manage and delete cookies and site data.

Consequences of Disabling Cookies: If you configure your browser to block all cookies, you will be unable to sign in to your MyJudicial account, access the client/advocate portal, manage bookings, or execute secure payments. Public browsing of advocate profiles and directory search will remain available.

sections.title: 10. Updates to This Cookie Policy
sections.text:
We may periodically update this Cookie Policy to reflect technical enhancements, architectural updates, or changes in applicable Rwandan regulations. When modifications occur, the "Last updated" date at the top of this document will be updated accordingly.

We encourage you to review this policy periodically to remain informed about our technical data practices.

faqs.title: Pricing & Payment FAQs
faqs.subtitle: Clear answers to common questions about fees, payments, and our escrow guarantee.
faqs.q1: How are legal service fees determined?
faqs.a1: Each certified advocate independently sets their fixed fees on MyJudicial based on their experience, specialty, and preparation required. Every service has a clearly stated scope and duration.
faqs.q2: Can I see the exact price before booking?
faqs.a2: Yes. You always see the complete fee in Rwandan Francs (RWF), the consultation duration, and the delivery mode before you confirm or authorize payment.
faqs.q3: What is included in the displayed price?
faqs.a3: The displayed fee covers the full consultation duration, pre-session brief review, encrypted video or phone connection, and secure escrow handling. There are no additional platform surcharges at checkout.
faqs.q4: Can a lawyer change the fee after I book?
faqs.a4: Never for an active booking. The price agreed at booking is legally binding for that session. If you subsequently decide to hire the advocate for ongoing courtroom litigation or separate casework, they will provide a distinct formal quotation.
faqs.q5: How does payment work via Mobile Money in Rwanda?
faqs.a5: We partner with AzamPay to provide direct Mobile Money checkout. When booking, enter your MTN (078/079) or Airtel (072/073) number. You will receive an instant USSD prompt on your phone to authorize the fee with your PIN.
faqs.q6: What does escrow mean on MyJudicial?
faqs.a6: Escrow means your money is not paid directly to the advocate upfront. Funds are held safely in platform custody until the consultation has taken place. The advocate is disbursed their payout only after session delivery.
faqs.q7: What happens if I need to cancel or the lawyer does not attend?
faqs.a7: If an advocate cancels or fails to attend, 100% of your funds are refunded immediately back to your Mobile Money account. You can also reschedule your session with the advocate prior to start time without penalty.
faqs.q8: Are there any hidden fees or extra invoices?
faqs.a8: None. MyJudicial eliminates unpredictable hourly meters, hidden retainers, and checkout processing surcharges. What you see is exactly what you pay.
